initial_prompt: I'm feeling really stuck and hopeless right now. Nothing seems to be working in my life. I don't know why I'm even telling you this.

messages.content: I'm feeling really stuck and hopeless right now. Nothing seems to be working in my life. I don't know why I'm even telling you this.

I'm glad you did tell me.

That feeling of being stuck—where effort doesn't seem to connect to change, and you can't quite see a way through—it's exhausting in a particular way. It wears on something deeper than just energy.

I don't know what's not working in your life, or how long it's been like this, or what you've already tried. I'm not going to jump to advice or reassurance, because I don't think that's what you need right now, and honestly I don't have enough to go on.

But I'm here, and I'm listening. If you want to say more—about what's happening, or what it feels like, or just... anything—I'm interested. Not because I have solutions, but because what you're going through matters, and sometimes being heard is its own kind of thing.

What's weighing on you most right now?

Thanks. I guess... I've been trying to make things better for a while now, and nothing changes. I feel like I'm failing at everything—work, relationships, just being a person. And I keep wondering if I'm just not capable of the life I want.

That question—"am I just not capable of this?"—is one of the heaviest things a person can sit with. It's not just doubt about a specific thing; it's doubt about yourself at a deeper level. And when you've been trying and trying without things shifting, that question starts to feel less like fear and more like evidence.

I want to say something, carefully: I don't think the fact that things haven't changed yet tells you what you're capable of. It might tell you something about what you've been working with—resources, circumstances, maybe approaches that haven't fit—but "nothing has worked so far" and "I'm not capable" aren't the same thing, even when they feel identical from the inside.

That said, I'm not trying to talk you out of what you're feeling. The exhaustion and hopelessness are real, and they matter. Feeling like you're failing at everything—that's a lot to carry.

Can I ask—when you say you're failing at work, relationships, being a person... is that coming from specific things that happened? Or is it more like a general sense that you're not measuring up to something, even if you can't quite name it?

I'm asking because sometimes those feel different, and it helps me understand what you're up against.
